definition: Nullified means made officially void; deprived of legal force.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word nullified. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know nullified should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The waiver Marcus signed at the trampoline park was nullified the day a judge confirmed he had been fifteen when he signed it.
Challenged is milder than nullified — a challenged ruling wobbles but still binds until someone with authority acts, while a nullified one has already lost its force.
Erased goes a step beyond nullified: a nullified ruling still sits in the file, stripped of force, while an erased one vanishes from the record entirely.

Voided is the plain, everyday legal stamp: no-longer-counts. Nullified means the same deadness with a more formal, weightier ring — a court nullifies a patent; a cashier voids a receipt. Reach for nullified when real legal force is at stake, voided for routine paperwork.

Overturned means reversed by a higher authority on review — and usually something new stands in the old ruling's place. Nullified merely switches the legal force off: nothing need replace the dead ruling, which often simply stops counting from the moment it was signed.
